urn:eigenius:core:description: A symbolic-algebra expression. Carries its term as a `formulas:FormulaTerm` value (D32 §4) — the shared formula language across every numerical institution. The Symbolics institution decodes the FormulaTerm into Symbolics.Num via the generated mirror, performs the requested operation (simplify, substitute, …), and re-encodes the result.

The expression's typed term — a FormulaTerm value (D32 §4). The chain validator type-checks the value against FormulaTerm's ctor schema at commit time; the mirror generator emits a typed Julia field whose value the worker decodes via `decode_FormulaTerm`.

Claim that one symbolic expression simplifies to another under the institution's pinned rewriter configuration. Validated by re-running `Symbolics.simplify` on the source side and confirming the result equals the claimed simplified form. `Holds` when the simplifier converges to the claimed form; `Undecidable` otherwise (Symbolics 7's `simplify` is heuristic — D27 §4.1.1 — so non-equality of simplified-form representations does not imply algebraic non-equivalence).
Source expression of a SimplifiesTo claim — the term whose simplified form the claim asserts.
Claimed simplified form of a SimplifiesTo claim — what the source expression is asserted to reduce to.

OnDemand input class for `qc_symb_simplify`: wraps a `SymbolicExpression` whose term will be re-run through `Symbolics.simplify`. The handler returns the simplified form as a fresh `SymbolicExpression`. The wrapper class exists because FIBER's institution-runtime boundary is unary — passing a SymbolicExpression directly via FIBER would force the user to construct a FormulaTerm value inline, which EigenQL's textual surface doesn't support; referencing a chain-committed SymbolicExpression by IRI through this wrapper is the natural shape.

Decidable input class for `qc_symb_check_equivalence`: pairs two `SymbolicExpression` resources and asks whether they are algebraically equivalent. The handler simplifies both sides under the institution's pinned rewriter and returns `Holds` on structural match, `Undecidable` otherwise (Symbolics' simplifier is heuristic — D27 §4.1.1). `Fails` is reserved for a future strict-decision path (groebner-basis / polynomial canonicalisation) that can refute equivalence on restricted fragments.
Left-hand symbolic expression of an equivalence check.
Right-hand symbolic expression of an equivalence check.
